content: Letter 19, to Amīrzāda Bāysunghur (ca. 826/1423?, Yazd?): an unusually long effusive letter. Ibn Turka describes attending the prince's court and conversing with its members when Bāysunghur rode in and, in the audience that followed, showed him particular favour. He calls himself a darvīsh who has suffered injustice and a broken stranger (MK: presumably referring to harassment by dīvān officials and enemies in Fars). He congratulates Bāysunghur on Shāhrukh's recent conquest (calling Shāhrukh emperor of Iran and Turan), says notables, religious leaders and scholars are hastening to court, and regrets that winter conditions prevent the month-long journey. He reminds the prince that some two months before, at the royal court, he had not been granted an audience with Shāhrukh but had been subjected to the attacks of fault-finders and defamers (TMN/MS pp. 14-17, TMN/D pp. 176-82).
